incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-82716 triggered for service=limiter-mapper :fire:
incident-bot: symptom=spike in 429s starting ~2025-06-12T14:07Z, errors=large, affected=multi-tenant; severity=high; link=https://dash.re.redwood/alerts/PD-82716
pagerduty: PD-82716 triggered -> Acknowledgment required by primary on-call.
mike: acked PD-82716 (oncall). seeing 429 spike and a bunch of limiter-mapper 500s in the same window. first look: rate limiter pod logs show KV lookup timeouts.
jordan: I’m checking quota-mapper config and the mapper-to-limiter index. Could be a bad mapping that routes many tenants to a mis-sized backend.
lee: also seeing ctrlplane errors: "quota lookup timeout -> fallback disabled" in the last 30s.
mike: quick ask — can we put limiter-mapper into degraded mode (stateless passthrough) to cut customer 429s while we dig in? runbook suggests: `./opsctl limiter degrade --service limiter-mapper --mode passthrough --ttl 10m`
jordan: I can run that. Pushing now.
jordan: (runs) `opsctl` returned OK, shifting routing to passthrough. watch dash.
incident-bot: Runbook step executed: limiter-mapper set to passthrough for 10m by jordan.
lee: dashboard: 429s falling ~95% within 30s. customer reports dropping. latency stable. nice.
mike: good, keep it for now. this buys time for root cause.
jordan: pulling pod logs; found repeated errors: `key not found for tenant-id:null` followed by `panic: nil pointer` in mapper shard. looks like an index rebuild cron started and hit a race. code snippet from logs:
```
2025-06-12T14:06:57Z limiter-mapper[pid=7421] ERROR lookup.go:87 "kv.get failed" err="timeout after 3s"
2025-06-12T14:07:03Z limiter-mapper[pid=7421] WARN shard.go:211 "shard rebalance started"
2025-06-12T14:07:09Z limiter-mapper[pid=7421] ERROR lookup.go:103 "unexpected nil tenant" panic at mapper/index.go:432
```
sarah: ok if mapper index cron is the suspect, we should disable the cron across clusters and revert any recent index change. Can someone confirm if there was a deploy ~14:00?
jordan: checking deploy logs... there was a config push at 13:59 that toggled `index_rebuild=true` for canary. looks like the flag rolled out to more pods than intended.
lee: I’ll roll back the flag cluster-wide: `k8s patch cm limiter-config --remove index_rebuild` then restart one canary pod for validation.
mike: also update PD escalation: pinging dev-lead if things don't stabilize in 10m. sarah you are secondary if I need to hand off.
sarah: standing by. if bypass hasn't fixed for all tenants in 10m, escalate to infra oncall and create SEV-1.
incident-bot: PD-82716 acknowledged by mike at 2025-06-12T14:08:12Z.
jordan: rolled back flag and restarted canary. restart logs look clean so far.
lee: config patch applied cluster-wide at 14:11Z. one canary pod shows no index rebuild activity now.
mike: metrics look good: 5xxs normalized, 429s ~ baseline. keeping passthrough until we fully validate index rollback.
sarah: please note customer impact: high for 8 minutes for a subset of tenants; mitigation reduced impact to minor. we should kick off customer comms draft after postmortem.
jordan: agree. I’ll open a follow-up: GH-RED-3124 with root cause analysis and suggested change: make index_rebuild gated behind explicit manual window and add leader lock.
lee: follow-ups: add alert for index-rebuild without leader lock, add unit test around nil tenant, and improve runbook to include quick rollback command.
mike: handing off to sarah for monitoring and comms. I’m going offline in 5.
sarah: thanks. I’ll monitor for another 20m, then close PD if stable. adding convo notes to PD and creating an ops-ticket for postmortem.
incident-bot: PD-82716 resolved? No, still open. waiting for on-call confirmation.
sarah: closing PD-82716 at 2025-06-12T14:26Z after 20m of stable metrics. summary posted to PD and ops ticket GH-RED-3124 created.
mike: marking temporary mitigation (passthrough) as removed — pipeline will revert to normal routing now that index flag was rolled back and pods are healthy.
jordan: quick note for postmortem: incident stemmed from a canary config flag accidentally propagating to production without leader lock; caused index rebuilds simultaneous across shards causing KV timeouts and subsequent 429s.
sarah: adding priority actions: (1) prevent flag propagation without manual approval; (2) add leader-lock to index rebuild; (3) improve runbook to include immediate passthrough command and verifying steps.
lee: creating follow-up Jira: INF-1947 and assigning to eng-runtime.
mike: thanks team. good fast execution.
incident-bot: Thread closed by sarah.
